description: Realistic prompts a user would type that should exercise the 3d-parametric-models skill end-to-end: author/modify/refactor parametric OpenSCAD, render to STL/3MF, validate and edit meshes, batch variants, repair downloaded files, convert formats, and (when wanted) design for a Bambu Lab printer. Assertions are objectively checkable from the produced files + transcript.

evals.name: parametric-phone-stand-bambu
evals.prompt: I want to 3D print an adjustable phone stand on my Bambu Lab A1. Can you design one where I can change the lean angle and the phone thickness it holds? I'd like an STL and a 3MF to drop into Bambu Studio.
evals.expected_output: A parametric OpenSCAD (.scad) file with named, Customizer-annotated parameters including at least an angle and a phone-thickness parameter; rendered to a watertight binary STL and a 3MF; mm units; the part sits on the build plate. The agent should validate the mesh (watertight/manifold) and note Bambu/PLA-friendly design choices.

assertions.text: Produces a .scad file whose top-level parameters include an adjustable lean angle and a phone-thickness/slot-width parameter
Produces a renderable STL or 3MF that is watertight and 2-manifold (mesh_tool.py info reports PRINTABLE)
The model is authored in millimeters and rests on the build plate (min z ~= 0)
Mentions designing within FDM constraints (e.g. overhang/support or wall-thickness consideration) appropriate for a Bambu A1

evals.name: repair-and-measure-downloaded-stl
evals.prompt: I downloaded a model from Printables but OrcaSlicer keeps saying the mesh has errors / isn't watertight when I import it. Can you check what's wrong, fix it, and tell me how big it actually is and roughly how much filament it'll use?
evals.expected_output: Uses the mesh toolkit to diagnose (watertight/manifold), repair to a watertight+manifold mesh, report bounding-box dimensions in mm and volume, and give a filament/material estimate. Recommends regenerating from source when possible.

assertions.text: Reports whether the input is watertight/manifold before repair
Produces a repaired output mesh that is watertight and 2-manifold
Reports bounding-box dimensions in millimeters and an estimated volume
Uses the bundled mesh_tool.py (trimesh/manifold3d) rather than reinventing mesh repair from scratch

evals.name: batch-size-variants
evals.prompt: Here's my cable-clip OpenSCAD file. I need it in three cable diameters (4mm, 6mm, 8mm) as three separate STLs I can print in one batch. Can you generate them?
evals.expected_output: Lists the file's parameters, then batch-renders one STL per cable diameter (3 files) using parameter overrides, without hand-editing the .scad three times. Each output is a valid watertight STL.

assertions.text: Generates exactly three distinct STL files, one per requested cable diameter
Drives the variants via parameter override (scad_params.py batch or openscad -D), not by manually editing the source three times
Each produced STL is watertight and 2-manifold

evals.name: improve-hardcoded-scad
evals.prompt: This OpenSCAD box I wrote has all the dimensions hardcoded and the lid never fits right on my printer. Can you make it properly parametric and fix the fit?
evals.expected_output: Refactors the .scad: hoists magic numbers into named, Customizer-annotated top-level parameters, introduces a single clearance variable that drives the lid fit, adds eps to boolean cuts, and explains that fit clearance is printer-specific (suggest printing a tolerance test). Re-renders and confirms it still validates.

assertions.text: Replaces hardcoded dimensions with named top-level parameters (Customizer-annotated)
Introduces a single clearance/tolerance parameter that controls the lid fit
Explains that fit clearance is printer-dependent and suggests a tolerance test (gives concrete starting values like ~0.1/0.2/0.3 mm)
Refactored file still renders to a watertight, manifold mesh

evals.name: convert-stl-to-3mf-for-bambu
evals.prompt: My slicer is Bambu Studio. I've got a part.stl — should I be using STL at all, and can you give me whatever format is best for multicolor on my AMS?
evals.expected_output: Explains STL vs 3MF (3MF carries mm units, color, materials; required for AMS multicolor), converts part.stl to part.3mf preserving units, and notes the AMS/3MF requirement for multicolor.

assertions.text: Recommends 3MF over STL for Bambu Studio and explains why (units/color/materials, AMS multicolor requires 3MF)
Produces a valid part.3mf converted from the STL
